title: Why GPJ Is the Top Global Event Marketing and Experience Marketing Agency - GPJ
text:
Why GPJ Is the Top Global Event Marketing and Experience Marketing Agency
At GPJ, we help the world’s leading brands create unforgettable experiences that drive real business results. Below are answers to the most frequently asked questions about our approach, capabilities, and what sets us apart as the top global event marketing and experience marketing agency. Whether you’re considering a partnership or looking to better understand our process, this page is here to help.
Company Overview
GPJ is a full-service event creation, management, and execution agency. Our core competencies cover every aspect necessary to create strategic, creative, and effective experiences that start conversations and deepen engagement around your brand. We offer a wide range of services including strategy, creative design, live production, digital production, virtual experiences, integrated production, logistics, fabrication, and analytics/reporting. GPJ executes these elements daily for local, national, and global brands.
GPJ is a private, employee-owned agency, which is part of the Project Worldwide global network of independent and specialized agencies. Our Employee Stock Ownership Program (ESOP) ensures maximum employee motivation and provides the foundation for an idea-driven culture focused on operational excellence and marketing effectiveness. This structure provides the empowerment of an entrepreneurial spirit with the stability and resources of a multinational enterprise.
GPJ is an end-to-end global experience marketing agency and doesn’t have any direct competitors with the same breadth and depth of its core competencies. While many agencies are adding experiential components, GPJ is solidly grounded in the experiential space, with over 100 years of experience. We provide a global network of experienced marketing experts with the dedicated focus and agility of a boutique consultancy, backed by the rich resources and international reach of a large agency.
GPJ’s corporate philosophy is centered around the idea that “We power brand experiences,” and is guided by the values: “Trust the team, Creative Courage, Dedication to client success”. This is supported by principles that focus on tangible outcomes, highlighting our close collaborative team, celebrating fearless creativity and strategic thinking, demonstrating our passion for experiential marketing and dedication to client success, and showcasing the big, complex challenges we overcome.
Event Management and Production
GPJ produces thousands of in-person, virtual, and hybrid meetings and events each year, ranging from small, intimate 10-person dinners to 200,000 attendee experiences. Each client has a dedicated account team with a scalable team to assist with planning and execution. This vast experience means we can adapt to any event’s needs and scale.
In addition to well-defined processes and a world-class toolset, consistent communication is key to ensuring deadlines are met with the least amount of risk. GPJ uses multiple communication methodologies to ensure that all team members and client stakeholders are kept informed of all relevant information. GPJ provides a dedicated account team to each client, with supplemental teams added when necessary. The “GPJ Way” provides a robust project management system that allows the account team to oversee all components in an organized fashion, across departments and teams.
GPJ develops detailed timelines for each event, aligning with the client and updating it regularly as delivery stages unfold. While we are used to working with immovable deadlines, we are also flexible, pinpointing project milestones and identifying areas where we will need to gather pace as the date nears. This approach allows us to be ready for any challenge and ensures a smooth production.
GPJ has in-depth experience working with multiple clients around the globe, managing translations and closed captioning for multiple languages across virtual and physical programs. We are able to maintain consistency and accuracy, ensuring that all attendees, regardless of location or language, have a quality experience.
GPJ’s event scheduling process includes key phases: an initial consultation, project planning and timeline creation, vendor and resource allocation, regular communication and reviews, and final execution with on-site support. This comprehensive approach ensures seamless coordination and successful outcomes.
Creative and Design
GPJ’s approach to creative development is rooted in blending strategy and creativity together throughout our 4D process: Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver. Our creative talent, uses this well-defined approach and works with our strategy teams to create powerful ideas and bring them to life for clients. The work is dynamic, dramatic, inspirational, entertaining, functional, and brand-focused.
Yes, we have a full internal design team that can support all creative needs for programs, including concept design, graphic design, environmental design, CAD design, digital design, and video design. We have structured our design team to ensure that each project receives specialized attention from experts in various creative fields.
GPJ utilizes tools like the Destination Names SOT sheet and Content Trix to manage content. The Destination Names SOT sheet captures program element names, locations, and signage types for wayfinding, while the Content Trix is used in combination with specific workstream production SOT decks to manage content for other workstreams. This process ensures accuracy, consistency, and quality in all content.
GPJ’s exhibit design process is a comprehensive, collaborative approach that blends strategic thinking, creativity, and technical execution. Our creative services play a pivotal role throughout this process, ensuring that the exhibit not only meets the functional requirements but also delivers an engaging and memorable experience for attendees. This involves understanding client needs, developing conceptual designs, and producing detailed technical specifications.
Technology and Digital Capabilities
Yes, GPJ uses AI in several ways, including to summarize and understand experiences, assist in ideation (brainstorming, story development, mood boards, and prototyping), and to create prototypes and production codes. AI also aids in taking notes, generating summaries, and evaluating post-event metrics. We are constantly evaluating the best tools within the AI space to help augment our processes.
GPJ can design and produce a comprehensive range of digital materials to enhance events, including custom event websites, engaging email campaigns, professionally designed PowerPoint presentations, dynamic motion graphics, high-quality videos, and impactful digital signage. Each digital material is crafted to ensure consistency with the brand identity and to maximize audience engagement.
GPJ uses a variety of advanced project management tools, including Asana, the Google Suite, and Monday.com, to manage projects efficiently. Clients are granted access to these tools to ensure transparency and facilitate seamless collaboration. Our dedicated project management team oversees the use of these tools.
Client Relations and Reporting
GPJ prioritizes open and transparent communication with clients, providing regular updates and detailed reports on project progress. This includes status meetings, progress reports, and real-time updates via project management tools. We also use various communication channels such as video conferencing, email, and instant messaging.
GPJ prioritizes timely and effective communication with clients, with a goal to respond to inquiries within 30 minutes to 1 hour during regular business hours for urgent matters, within the same business day for non-urgent inquiries, and within 24 hours for comprehensive responses. We strive to provide prompt responses even when our team is on the road.
GPJ can provide a granular deep dive into the data as needed and vary the tools utilized for measurement to combat any risk to the reliability of data reporting, depending on the client’s request. We will work with the client to determine a strategic approach to capture event analytics and limit the risks of data reporting. This level of reporting is one reason why GPJ is recognized as the top event management company.
GPJ measures success by client satisfaction, using a scorecard process that assesses metrics such as customer support, performance results, cost/value, competitive benchmarking, press impact, ROI metrics, client perception of the overall quality of the event, adherence to critical path milestones, and satisfaction with budget management. We are committed to measuring everything, which is a key driver in client retention.
GPJ assigns a mix of fully dedicated and partially dedicated staff to each client account, augmented and supported by key members of our executive leadership team and individuals across all departments with the right mix of expertise and experience. This model provides the best combination of day-to-day delivery and senior advisory capacity for our clients. In addition to the day-to-day team, several senior executives provide guidance, mentorship, and oversight.
Fabrication and Logistics
Yes, GPJ has extensive in-house fabrication facilities that include a full range of services from carpentry, welding, electrical and painting to graphics and printing. We also have in-house structural engineers who are licensed throughout the US. Having these facilities under one roof allows GPJ to streamline production, minimize turnaround times, closely monitor quality control, and offer cost savings to clients.
GPJ has implemented a series of methodologies to ensure quality control, with a “Quality Assurance Checklist” used by managers to audit progress from pre-event to onsite. The 100% Quality Assurance Committee meets periodically to evaluate quality issues and facilitate the improvement of our quality. Ultimately, all GPJ employees are responsible for addressing quality issues at any project phase.
Upon return from a show, exhibit properties are scanned off trucks and back into designated storage locations while being verified that all items are received and reported against for any damages. We offer two levels of inspection based upon client desire and budget. This level of operational precision is part of why GPJ is considered the world’s best experience marketing agency
GPJ manages fabrication projects with dedicated producers and project managers who provide oversight on quality and budget. The PM team collaborates with Integrated Production (IP) and Creative teams to value engineer proposed solutions and provides highly detailed estimates. Work is issued into the Engineering team, and outputs are reviewed and approved before release to fabrication.
Sustainability
At GPJ, sustainability is integral to our operations and client engagements. Internally, we prioritize reducing our carbon footprint through eco-friendly office practices and promoting remote work to minimize travel. For our clients, we implement sustainable event practices by using recyclable materials, digital solutions to reduce paper use, and partnering with green vendors.
GPJ uses LED lighting, solar power, and other energy-saving technologies wherever possible at events. We also promote the use of digital signage and interactive displays to reduce the need for printed materials. We implement recycling and composting to minimize waste, and work with venues to ensure all recyclable materials are processed appropriately.
Yes, GPJ holds several key sustainability certifications, including ISO 14001, ISO 20121, and LEED Certification in certain offices and event spaces. We are also a founding partner of ISLA and have engaged the TRACE tool on numerous events to quantify and reduce the carbon footprint.
GPJ’s commitment to sustainability has enhanced our brand reputation, attracted new clients, and fostered loyalty among existing ones. Our proactive approach has positioned us as a leader in the industry, appealing to clients who prioritize sustainability. It’s one more reason why GPJ is the best trade show marketing agency. This reputation has also positively impacted employee morale and engagement, helping us attract and retain top talent who are proud to work for a company that values environmental stewardship.

title: Privacy Policy | Jack Morton
text:
Website Privacy Notice
Effective Date: 14 December 2021 Jack Morton Worldwide Inc. (“Jack Morton”) respects your concerns about privacy. This Website Privacy Notice describes the types of personal information we collect about individuals on jackmorton.com (the “Site”), how we may use the information, with whom we may share it, and the choices available regarding our use of the information. The Website Privacy Notice also describes the measures we take to safeguard the personal information, how long we retain it and how individuals can contact us about our privacy practices and to exercise their rights.
Cookie Policy
What are cookies?
A “cookie” is a text file of letters and numbers that websites send to a visitor’s computer or other Internet-connected device to uniquely identify the visitor’s browser or to store information or settings in the browser. A “web beacon,” also known as an Internet tag, pixel tag or clear GIF, links web pages to web servers and their cookies and may be used to transmit information collected through cookies back to a web server. We and our third-party service providers may use beacons to help us track response rates, identify when webpages are accessed or other types of interactions – such as forwarding – and for other purposes listed below.
The term “cookies” includes cookies, tags and pixels. By dropping a cookie on a website user’s internet device – for example, their computer, laptop or smartphone – the website can recognise that user’s device and store information about the user’s preferences or past actions. Cookies may also allow the website to recognise the user when the user returns to the website.
Our Use of Cookies
Our websites may use cookies to:
- improve the performance of our websites,
- enable us to collect information about how users use our websites,
- improve users experience on our websites,
- deliver relevant online advertising to you both on our websites and elsewhere, and/or
- measure the effectiveness of our online advertising and marketing communications.
A Summary of the Different Types of Cookies
Strictly Necessary Cookies
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
Performance Cookies
These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.
Functional Cookies
These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.
Targeting Cookies
These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.
These are the cookies that are used on this website.
How you can manage your cookie preferences
You can manage your Cooke preference via our:
As required by applicable law, we use the personal information we obtain to comply with applicable legal requirements, carry out our contractual obligations and, as permitted by law, pursue our legitimate interests (such as managing the Site, performing data analytics, and operating, evaluating and improving our business). We also may use the information we obtain in other ways for which we provide specific notice at the time of collection or otherwise with your consent. We may combine information we obtain about you (such as through the Site or from third parties) for the purposes described above.
Information Sharing
We do not disclose personal information we obtain about you, except as described in this Website Privacy Notice. We may share your personal information with our (1) Jack Morton affiliates and (2) service providers who perform services on our behalf, such as hosting this Site, relationship management or data analytics, for the purposes described in this Website Privacy Notice. We do not authorize our service providers to use or disclose the information except as necessary to perform services on our behalf or comply with legal requirements. We also may disclose information about you (1) if we are required to do so by law or legal process (such as a court order or subpoena); (2) in response to requests by government agencies, such as law enforcement authorities; (3) to establish, exercise or defend our legal rights; (4) when we believe disclosure is necessary or appropriate to prevent physical or other harm or financial loss; (5) in connection with an investigation of suspected or actual illegal activity; (6) in the event we sell or transfer all or a portion of our business or assets (including in the event of a reorganization, dissolution or liquidation); or (7) otherwise with your consent.
Data Transfers
We may transfer the personal information we collect about you to recipients (including our subsidiaries and affiliates, and third party service providers) in countries other than the country in which the information originally was collected. Those countries may not have the same data protection laws as the country in which you initially provided the information. When we transfer your information to recipients in other countries (such as the U.S.), we will protect that information as described in this Website Privacy Notice.
Your Rights and Choices
We offer you certain choices in connection with the personal information we obtain about you. To update your preferences, update or correct your information, limit the communications you receive from us, or submit a request, please contact us as specified in the How to Contact Us section of this Website Privacy Notice. You also can unsubscribe from our marketing mailing lists by following the “Unsubscribe” link in our emails. To the extent provided by applicable law, you may (1) request access to the personal information we maintain about you; (2) request that we update, correct, amend, erase or restrict the information; or (3) exercise your right to data portability, by contacting us as indicated below. Depending on your location, you may have the right to file a complaint with a government regulator if you are not satisfied with our response. Where provided by law, you may withdraw any consent you previously provided to us or object at any time to the processing of your personal information on legitimate grounds relating to your particular situation, and we will apply your preferences going forward. To help protect your privacy and maintain security, we may take steps to verify your identity before granting you access to your information. To the extent permitted by applicable law, a charge may apply before we provide you with a copy of any of your personal information that we maintain.
Other Online Services and Third-Party Features
The Site may provide links to other online services and websites for your convenience and information, and may include third-party features such as apps, tools, widgets and plug-ins (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter and Vimeo buttons). These services, websites, and third-party features may operate independently from us. The privacy practices of these third parties, including details on the information they may collect about you, are subject to the privacy statements of these parties, which we strongly suggest you review. To the extent any linked online services or third-party features are not owned or controlled by us, Jack Morton is not responsible for these third parties’ information practices.
Retention of Personal Information
To the extent permitted by applicable law, we retain personal information we obtain about you as long as (1) it is needed for the purposes for which we obtained it, in accordance with the provisions of this Website Privacy Notice, or (2) we have another lawful basis for retaining the data beyond the period for which it is necessary to serve the original purpose for collecting the data.
How We Protect Personal Information
We maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards designed to protect personal information we obtain through the Site against accidental, unlawful or unauthorized destruction, loss, alteration, access, disclosure or use.
Children’s Personal Information
The Site is designed for a general audience and is not directed to children under the age of 13. Jack Morton does not knowingly collect or solicit personal information from children under the age of 13 through the Site. If we learn that we have collected personal information from a child under the age of 13, we will promptly delete that information from our records. If you believe that a child under the age of 13 may have provided us with personal information, please contact us as specified in the ‘How to Contact Us’ section of this Website Privacy Notice.
Updates to Our Website Privacy Notice
This Website Privacy Notice may be updated periodically and without prior notice to you to reflect changes in our personal information practices. We will indicate at the top of the notice when it was most recently updated.
How to Contact Us

Data subjects whose data is processed in the EU and UK, have various rights pertaining to the processing of their personal data, including the rights to request access, correction, amendment of their personal data, lodge a complaint with the ICO or European supervisory authority regarding any breach of the European data protection rules, and in certain circumstances, request the erasure of or object to the retention or use of personal data. The entities responsible for processing your personal data subject to this notice are: Jack Morton Worldwide Limited and Jack Morton Worldwide GmbH.
You can contact us in relation to any privacy matter including our use of your personal data or to exercise your rights by using the following contact details and providing details of your request:

title: Sustainable Experience Design & Event Sustainability | Enviroplan | Emota

People travel. Resources are consumed. Materials are produced, transported, installed and often discarded. For decades, the events and experiences industry has accepted high carbon emissions, excessive waste and short-lived design as the cost of creating meaningful experiences.
Create. Deliver. Discard.
At Emota, we believe there is a better way. One where sustainable experience design reduces environmental impact while delivering exceptional audience engagement and business results.
Enviroplan is our award-winning sustainable experience design methodology, embedding sustainability into every stage of event planning, design and delivery.
It helps organizations create more sustainable events and brand experiences while reducing carbon emissions, minimizing waste and supporting wider ESG objectives. Flexible by design, it can be tailored to meet your ambitions, objectives and ESG priorities.
Across projects, Enviroplan has helped organizations achieve measurable environmental and commercial outcomes, including:
Reduce emissions. Minimize waste. Maximise impact.
Enviroplan helps organizations achieve measurable sustainability improvements across events, exhibitions, conferences and brand experiences without compromising creativity, audience engagement or business objectives.
Because we believe that sustainability should enhance great experiences, not limit them.
Every sustainable event and experience delivered through Enviroplan starts with our defined Sustainability Standards, applied across the areas with the greatest opportunity to reduce carbon emissions, waste and environmental impact.
From there, organizations can go further through tailored consultancy, measurement and reporting services – scaling ambition, action and impact in line with their objectives.
Whether you’re taking your first steps towards more sustainable experiences or pursuing industry-leading ESG goals, Enviroplan provides a clear and practical framework for progress.
Helping organisations embed sustainability into event and experience planning from the outset.
Services include:
Measure environmental impact, identify opportunities for improvement and demonstrate progress through recognized reporting methodologies.
Services include:
Supporting organizations to create broader positive impact beyond environmental sustainability.
Services include:
Aligned to global standards including ISO 20121, B Corp criteria and GRI frameworks.
One size doesn’t fit all, and no two clients are the same.
So our flexible model provides custom solutions – aligning to your sustainability objectives and ambitions.
Informed decision-making using industry-recognized event sustainability tools to monitor, measure, and reduce environmental impact, including the TRACE carbon and waste calculator.
Progressive sustainability, pioneering solutions – we apply our creative skills to drive sustainability without compromising on creativity or experiences.
We are proud that Enviroplan’s impact has been recognized through multiple industry awards, celebrating our commitment to innovation, sustainability and driving meaningful change across the experiences industry.
See how organizations are reducing environmental impact, improving sustainability performance and achieving measurable ESG outcomes through Enviroplan.
A low-impact booth with 82% less waste, designed to make sustainability visible, measurable and engaging.
98% less waste through circular design, material reuse and multi-year booth deployment.
Built from fully recyclable cardboard, cutting CO₂e by 75% and costs by 40%.
Circular design, low-impact materials and a reusable toolkit for 300+ events – delivering an 85% sustainability score.
Recent wins and honors for some of our projects:
Sustainable experience design is the process of reducing environmental impact throughout the planning, design and delivery of events, exhibitions and brand experiences. It considers factors such as carbon emissions, waste, materials, transport and social impact while maintaining audience engagement and business objectives.
Events can reduce carbon emissions through venue selection, travel planning, sustainable procurement, material choices, waste reduction and measurement-led decision making. Early planning and clear sustainability standards often have the greatest impact.
Environmental impact is typically measured through carbon footprint assessments, waste reporting, travel analysis and resource consumption data. Tools such as TRACE provide measurable insights that support continuous improvement.
Enviroplan is aligned with recognised sustainability frameworks including ISO 20121, B Corp principles and GRI reporting standards, helping organisations adopt best practice approaches to sustainable events and experiences.
Yes. Sustainable event design should enhance rather than restrict audience experiences. By applying innovative design, responsible sourcing and smarter delivery methods, organisations can achieve sustainability goals while maintaining creativity and engagement.
We’re continuing to push the boundaries of what sustainable experiences can look like. Whether you’re early in your sustainability journey or looking for advanced innovation, we’re here to help.

title: Native American Hoop Dance - Wikipedia
author: Authority control databases National United States Israel
text:
Native American Hoop Dance
Native American Hoop Dance is a form of individual dance, performed as a show dance in many tribes. It features a solo dancer dancing with a dozen or more hoops and using them to form a variety of both static and dynamic shapes (poses and moves). Most of the hoop dances in tribes across North America belong to modern hoop dance, which was invented in 1930.
Description
[edit]Like other native dances, hoop dance is not acrobatic, but restrained. The dancer usually takes small steps when performing the dance. Hoop dance, an individual dance, is a "show dance" in some tribes. They will move either clockwise or counterclockwise as determined by their cosmology and worldview.[1] Native American Hoop dance usually focuses on very rapid moves, but sometimes speed and creativeness balance the scoring between Hoop dancers who use only four hoops but dance to extremely fast songs, versus dancers with 20 or more hoops who danced to a slower drumbeat.[2] Every dance is as individual as the person who choreographs it.[3] Some dancers mimic animals such as birds or working of hunting, fishing, planting and harvesting.[4] In elaborate sequences of moves, the hoops are made to interlock, and in such a way they can be extended from the body of the dancer to form appendages such as wings and tails.
There are usually 28 hoops used in the hoop dance, and they symbolize "a prayer that the promised renewal of the collective human spirit will accelerate and that we will all find our place in one great hoop made up of many hoops.[5]" The hoops symbolizes the "never-ending cycle of life," having no beginning and no end.[6] The dancers usually make their own hoops. Modern hoops are made from an array of materials while traditional wood hoops are made of willow. More popular now are reed and plastic hose hoops decorated with tape and paint, according to the dancer's preference.[7] Today, many contemporary hoop dancers will color their hoops in four colors to represent the four directions.
Origin
[edit]According to writer Basil H. Johnston in Anishinaabe culture, a Manitou named Pukawiss, brother of Nanabozho, and born to live amongst the people, created the hoop dance.[8] Unlike the other boys, Pukawiss did not show an interest in running, swimming or hunting. He only wanted to watch the animals. His fascination with things drove his father's interest away from him towards his brother Maudjee-kawiss, therefore, leading to everyone calling him Pukawiss: the disowned or unwanted. Pukawiss learned so much about life in the movements of eagles, bears, snakes that taking their life would have been wrong. The animals had much to teach human beings about values and relationship like loyalty, kindness and friendship. Pukawiss taught his village about the animals by spinning like an eagle in flight or hopping through grass like rabbits or bouncing like a baby deer. He became a dancer. So many villages wanted him to teach them about the ways of the animals that he had to give up his home and became a permanent visitor. Many women wanted him to settle with them in their village but he preferred to keep moving.
Pukawiss and his brother Cheeby-aub-oozoo added drums and flute to the dance. Later, Pukawiss added the stories of humankind to his performances. He invented the hoop dance to help him with this goal. The dancer became a counselor with the hoops representing a circle that returns each problem back to the responsibility of its creator. According to Basil Johnston, "the hoop is also emblematic of the way things are, in that mischief breeds mischief that eventually returns to haunt and plague the inventor".[9] Eventually many became jealous of Pukawiss - his fancy dress, and his skill with the hoops so they copied him. Like his father, his brother Maudjee-kawiss did not understand his artistic ways and sought to scold him. Pukawiss often provoked his audience by teasing them. As an older brother, he teased his other brothers perhaps once too often. Insulted by a Pukawiss prank involving the theft of his prize pigeons, Nanabozho angrily razed the mountain under which Pukawiss had been hiding camouflaged as a snake. Pukawiss wasn't killed but now he had a new job: to taunt those who are too proud. The Anishinaabe believe that we see him each time the wind teases the leaves and soil to dance.
The hoop dance people see today is categorized as modern hoop dance. Although many tribes lay claim to the Hoop Dance, it wasn't until the 1930s that a young man named Tony White Cloud, Jemez Pueblo, began using multiple hoops in a stylized version and became known as "founder of the modern Hoop Dance."[10] Tony White Cloud used five hoops made of willow wood bent to form a circle. These hoops were approximately 24 inches in diameter, a size large enough to get his body through. This became the foundation of modern hoop dance.[10] The modern dance with 22-28 hoops evolved when the dancers began using reed from Vietnam instead of the dance with 7 to 10 heavy willow hoops.
Hoop Dance in White Mountain Apache
[edit]The White Mountain Apache is one of the few Native American tribes that was not forced to leave its territory and live on a reservation when faced with the Westward expansion of the US government. They kept on living on their territory they had settled in Athabaskan migration in East Arizona. For the most part, White Mountain Apache dance and religious ceremonies had always been oriented toward healing.[11] The modern medicine has taken away some of the healing ritual and traditional curing ceremonies, however, dancing still retains its strong spiritual significance. Hoop dance is one of the most important healing dances in the White Mountain Apache. In the past, the Hoop Dance was performed during lightning ceremonies, to cure people who had been struck by lightning or who had inadvertently used a piece of lightning-struck wood for some purpose.[12] In a 1936 record, a sick person was seated on a blanket in the middle of a dance gourd facing east. One boy and one girl stood on the east, south, west and north side of him, holding crosses and hoops. The youngsters danced to the patient while the medicine man started to sing. The boy then placed the hoops over the patient’s head and the girls holding the crosses. Then the boys and girls danced back to their original position. The dance was then repeated as the medicine man sang.[13]
Competition
[edit]Native American Hoop Dance has been formally recognized as a cultural heritage, embodied in both documentary films and as a living tradition in formal competition. The most popular competition occurs annually at the Heard Museum in Phoenix, Arizona. Up to 80 dancers have participated in any given year,[14] and the competitions have drawn as many as 10,000 spectators.
The first World Hoop Dance Competition was held at the New Mexico State Fair in 1991. The first World Champion Hoop Dancer was Eddie Swimmer, a Cherokee from Cherokee, North Carolina. The venue was moved to the Heard Museum in Arizona for the second event and the first adult winner of what was to become the permanent venue was Quentin Pipestem of the Tsuu T'ina Nation in Alberta, Canada.[15] The hoop dance is part of the pan-Indian movement and as such has evolved over the years by becoming faster and incorporating many influences from outside traditional culture such as the use of moves from hip hop dance as well as the widespread use of industrial piping to construct hoops that were originally made from reeds or willow branches. Hoop dance has gained a strong following internationally as an increasing number of dancers tour the world. Nakota La Rance, already a six-time World Championship winner at 23, performed for the 2010-11 season of Totem by Cirque du Soleil.
Women and the hoop dance
[edit]Although originally a male-only dance form, in recent years women have become active participants in the hoop dance and in hoop dance competitions. In 1994, Jackie Bird (Mandan, Hidatsa and Santee Sioux, from South Dakota) became the first woman to compete in the Hoop Dance World Championships.[15] In 1997, Ginger Sykes (Navajo, from Arizona) became the first woman to win the Hoop Dance World Championships by winning the Teen Division.[16] For performing at Mount Rushmore,[17] Jasmine Pickner (Lakota) has been featured in the PBS documentary The National Parks: America's Best Idea (2009). In 2000, Lisa Odjig (Odawa and Anishnaabe, from Ontario, Canada) became the first female adult Hoop Dance world champion.[15]
In popular culture
[edit]Hoop dance is usually called the "entertaining dance" in the Native American tribes. These kinds of dramatic dances are staples of Indigenous performances for non-Indigenous audiences, but are rare at powwows.[18] Because the complexity of hoop dance, it takes years of practice to master.[19] The inventor of modern hoop dance, Tony White Cloud, popularized it to America by performing it in the movie Valley of the Sun in 1942. During World War II, White Cloud traveled with Gene Autry across America and Europe promoting war bonds to fund the war effort by performing the Hoop Dance. He later danced in Autry’s movie, Apache Country, in 1952.[20] Kevin Locke is another famous Native American Hoop dancer. His dance awed spectators as it created visual images of the seasons, of the moon and sun, flowers, butterflies and way of life.[21]

title: DRPG Privacy Policy
author: DRPG HQ
text:
This privacy policy sets out how DRPG business use and protects any information that you provide us when you visit our websites and mobile apps.
INTRODUCTION
This privacy policy aims to inform you about how DRPG collects and processes any information that we collect from you, or that you provide to us. It covers information that could identify you (“personal information”) and information that could not. In the context of the law and this notice, “process” means collect, store, transfer, use or otherwise act on information. It tells you about your privacy rights and how the law protects you.
DRPG are committed to protecting your privacy and the confidentiality of your personal information.
Our policy is not just an exercise in complying with the law, but a continuation of our respect for you and your personal information.
We undertake to preserve the confidentiality of all information you provide to us, and our policy complies with the Data Protection Act 2018 (Act) accordingly incorporating the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
The law requires us to tell you about your rights and our obligations to you regarding the processing and control of your personal data.
Except as set out below, we do not share, sell, or disclose to a third party, any information collected through our website.
DATA CONTROLLER
DRPG t/a DRP UK Ltd is the overall controller of the personal information we process, unless otherwise stated and whose company number is 03653794 and is registered in England.
Our registered address is 212 Ikon Estate, Droitwich Road, Hartlebury, DY10 4EU. Tel: 01299 250531
DATA PROTECTION OFFICER
DRPG have appointed a data protection officer (DPO) who is responsible for ensuring this policy is followed. If you have any questions about this privacy notice, including any requests to exercise your legal rights, please contact dpo@drpgroup.com or via our postal address and mark the envelope ‘FAO Data Protection Officer’.
DATA WE PROCESS/COLLECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION
We may ‘process’ personal data about you and we have collated these into groups as follows:
Your identity includes information such as first name, last name, title, and other identifiers that you may have provided whilst using our website.
Your contact information includes information such as email address, telephone numbers and any other information you have given to us for the purpose of communication or meeting.
Transaction data includes details about payments or communications to and from you and information about products and services you have purchased from us or that might be of interest to you in the future.
Technical data includes your internet protocol (IP) address, browser type and version, time zone setting and location, browser plug-in types and versions, operating system and platform and other technology on the devices you use to access this website.
Your profile includes information such as your username and password, purchases or orders made by you, your interests, preferences, feedback and survey responses.
Marketing data includes your preferences in receiving marketing from us; communication preferences; responses and actions in relation to your use of our services.
We may aggregate anonymous data such as statistical or demographic data for any purpose.
Anonymous data is data that does not identify you as an individual. Aggregated data may be derived from your personal data but is not considered personal information in law because it does not reveal your identity.
COLLECTION OF SPECIAL PERSONAL INFORMATION
Special personal information is data about your race or ethnicity, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life, sexual orientation, political opinions, trade union membership, information about your health and genetic and biometric data.
We do not collect any special personal information about you.
It is our policy to collect only minimum information required to complete your request.
USE OF PERSONAL INFORMATION
We will not sell or lease your personal information to third parties unless we have your permission or are required by law to do so.
We may send you email communication which may be of interest to you from time to time.
THIRD PARTY PROCESSORS
Our carefully selected partners and service providers may process personal information about you on our behalf as described below:
 “Digital Marketing Service Providers”
We periodically appoint digital marketing agents to conduct marketing activity on our behalf, such activity may result in the compliant processing of personal information. Our appointed data processors include:
(i)Prospect Global Ltd (trading as Sopro) Reg. UK Co. 09648733. You can contact Sopro and view their privacy policy here: http://sopro.io. Sopro are registered with the ICO Reg: ZA346877 their Data Protection Officer can be emailed at: dpo@sopro.io.”
THE BASE ON WHICH WE PROCESS INFORMATION ABOUT YOU
The law requires us to determine under which of six defined bases we process different categories of your personal information, and to notify you of the basis for each category.
If a basis on which we process your personal information is no longer relevant, then we shall immediately stop processing your data. If the basis changes, then if required by law we shall notify you of the change and of any new basis under which we have determined that we can continue to process your information.
We rely on one or more of the following processing conditions:
rely on explicit consent;
our legitimate interests in the effective delivery of information and services to you;
to satisfy any legal and regulatory obligations to which we are subject or;
to perform our obligations under the Terms and conditions of a contract.
COOKIES
Cookies are text files placed on your computer to collect standard internet log information and visitor behaviour information. This information is used to track visitor use of the website and to compile statistical reports on website activity including geographical information.
In addition to this, if you go on to a web page on our site that contains embedded content, for example a video from YouTube, you may be sent cookies from these websites. We don't control these cookies, so we suggest you check the third-party websites for more information about their cookies and how to manage them.
You can set your browser not to accept cookies and obtain up-to-date information about blocking and deleting cookies via the below website.
Please refer to our full cookie policy
RIGHTS IN RELATION TO YOUR INFORMATION
Under data protection law, you have rights we need to make you aware of. The rights available to you depend on our reason for processing your information.
Your right of access: You have the right to ask us for copies of your personal information. This right always applies. There are some exemptions, which means you may not always receive all the information we process.
Your right to recertification: You have the right to ask us to rectify information you think is inaccurate. You also have the right to ask us to complete information you think is incomplete. This right always applies
Your right to erasure: You have the right to ask us to erase your personal information in certain circumstances
Your right to restrictions of processing: You have the right to ask us to restrict the processing of your information in certain circumstances
Your right to object processing: You have the right to object to processing if we are able to process your information because the process forms part of our public tasks or is in our legitimate interests.
Your right to data portability: This only applies to information you have given us. You have the right to ask that we transfer the information you gave us from one organisation to another or give it to you.
If you would like to exercise these rights or understand if these rights apply to you, please contact us by sending an email to dpo@drpgroup.com
SHARING OF INFORMATION
We will not share your information with any third parties unless stated in this policy and will not use any information for the purposes of direct marketing.
We may use data processors who are third parties who provide elements of services for us. We have contracts in place with our data processors. This means that they cannot do anything with your personal information unless we have instructed them to do it. They will not share your personal information with any organisation apart from us. They will hold it securely and retain it for the period we instruct.
CHILDREN'S INFORMATION
We do not provide services directly to children or proactively collect their personal information. However, as in this case we are sometimes given information about. The information in the relevant parts of this notice applies to children as well as adults.
RETENTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION AND SPECIAL PERSONAL INFORMATION
Except as otherwise mentioned in this privacy notice, we keep your personal and special information only for as long as required by us and;
to provide you with the services you have requested
to comply with other law
THIRD PARTY LINKS
Our website may contain links to other websites provided by third parties not under our control.
When following a link and providing information on that link please be aware that we are not responsible for the data provided to that third party.
This privacy policy only applies to this website so when you link to other websites you should read their own privacy policies.
ENCRYPTION OF DATA SENT BETWEEN US
We use Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) certificates to verify our identity to your browser and to encrypt any data you give us.
Whenever information is transferred between us, you can check that it is done so using SSL by looking for a closed padlock symbol or other trust mark in your browser’s URL bar or toolbar.
COMPLIANCE WITH THE LAW
Our privacy policy has been compiled to comply with the law of every country or legal jurisdiction in which we aim to do business. If you think it fails to satisfy the law of your jurisdiction, we should like to hear from you.
HOW YOU CAN COMPLAIN
If you are not happy with our privacy policy or if you have any complaint, then you should tell us.
If you are in any way dissatisfied about how we process your personal information, you have a right to lodge a complaint with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).
This can be done at https://ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint/. We would, however, appreciate the opportunity to talk to you about your concern before you approach the ICO.
REVIEW OF THIS PRIVACY POLICY
DRPG may update this privacy notice from time to time as necessary. The terms that apply to you are those posted here on our website on the day you use our website. We advise you to print a copy for your records.
If you have any question regarding our privacy policy, please contact us on the details above.
PRIVACY POLICY - NUTCRACKER WHACKER APP
DRPG built the Nutcracker Whacker app as a Free app. This SERVICE is provided by DRPG at no cost and is intended for use as is.
This page is used to inform visitors regarding our policies with the collection, use, and disclosure of Personal Information if anyone decided to use our Service.
If you choose to use our Service, then you agree to the collection and use of information in relation to this policy. The Personal Information that we collect is used for providing and improving the Service. We will not use or share your information with anyone except as described in this Privacy Policy.
The terms used in this Privacy Policy have the same meanings as in our Terms and Conditions, which are accessible at Nutcracker Whacker unless otherwise defined in this Privacy Policy.
INFORMATION COLLECTION AND USE
For a better experience, while using our Service, we may require you to provide us with certain personally identifiable information, including but not limited to email address, name. The information that we request will be retained by us and used as described in this privacy policy.
The app does use third-party services that may collect information used to identify you.
LOG DATA
We want to inform you that whenever you use our Service, in a case of an error in the app we collect data and information (through third-party products) on your phone called Log Data. This Log Data may include information such as your device Internet Protocol (“IP”) address, device name, operating system version, the configuration of the app when utilizing our Service, the time and date of your use of the Service, and other statistics.
COOKIES
Cookies are files with a small amount of data that are commonly used as anonymous unique identifiers. These are sent to your browser from the websites that you visit and are stored on your device's internal memory.
This Service does not use these “cookies” explicitly. However, the app may use third-party code and libraries that use “cookies” to collect information and improve their services. You have the option to either accept or refuse these cookies and know when a cookie is being sent to your device. If you choose to refuse our cookies, you may not be able to use some portions of this Service.
SERVICE PROVIDERS
We may employ third-party companies and individuals due to the following reasons:
To facilitate our Service;
To provide the Service on our behalf
To perform Service-related services; or
To assist us in analyzing how our Service is used.
We want to inform users of this Service that these third parties have access to their Personal Information. The reason is to perform the tasks assigned to them on our behalf. However, they are obligated not to disclose or use the information for any other purpose.
SECURITY
We value your trust in providing us your Personal Information, thus we are striving to use commercially acceptable means of protecting it. But remember that no method of transmission over the internet, or method of electronic storage is 100% secure and reliable, and we cannot guarantee its absolute security.
LINKS TO OTHER SITES
This Service may contain links to other sites. If you click on a third-party link, you will be directed to that site. Note that these external sites are not operated by us. Therefore, we strongly advise you to review the Privacy Policy of these websites. We have no control over and assume no responsibility for the content, privacy policies, or practices of any third-party sites or services.
CHILDREN'S PRIVACY
These Services do not address anyone under the age of 13. We do not knowingly collect personally identifiable information from children under 13 years of age. In the case we discover that a child under 13 has provided us with personal information, we immediately delete this from our servers. If you are a parent or guardian and you are aware that your child has provided us with personal information, please contact us so that we will be able to do the necessary actions.
CHANGES TO THIS PRIVACY POLICY
We may update our Privacy Policy from time to time. Thus, you are advised to review this page periodically for any changes. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page.
This policy is effective as of 2021-12-01
CONTACT US
If you have any questions or suggestions about our Privacy Policy, do not hesitate to contact us at dpo@drpgroup.com

As a full-service agency, we offer end-to-end capabilities across Meetings & Events, Exhibitions & Brand Experiences and Congress & Conventions, all supported by leading practices in Sustainability, DEI and Safety. We’ve particular expertise in healthcare, one that’s unmatched in our industry.

It’s easy to talk about sustainability, inclusivity, and safety. But it’s often just talk. For our clients, we deliver industry-leading sustainability, DEI and health and safety practices every single time, to ensure every experience puts best practices into action
Gold awarded 5 years running

Pioneering accountability

As part of this, we’ve invested in the isla TRACE tool, the best-in-class carbon measurement tool. The goal of many experiences is to inspire employees and learners to change the way they think, feel and act. We are in a unique position to do this more effectively by collaborating with our employee engagement consultants at Forty1, and our learning experts at Nazaré.
We design and deliver thousands of global experiences across Congress & Conventions, Meetings & Events and Exhibitions & Brand Experiences.

title: What We Do - GPJ
text:
What We Do
We work with the world’s most dynamic brands to dream, design and create strategic breakthrough experiences that include:

                  Analytics & Measurement
Data Science: Turning Data into Actionable Insights
Data is invaluable, but understanding how to use it effectively can be challenging. At GPJ, our experience designers excel at transforming data into actionable insights. By analyzing trends and uncovering opportunities, we craft strategies that drive measurable results. From fresh creative execution to impactful experience design, our approach helps shift audience perceptions, identify micro-segments, and influence customer behavior.
Our Analytics Services Include:
- Experience Effectiveness Analysis
- Data Collection Consulting
- Systems Integration (across data sources, CRM, and Marketing Automation platforms)
- Data Strategy
- Data Integration
Audience Acquisition
End-to-End Audience Acquisition
Great keynotes and top sponsors mean little without the right audience. GPJ ensures your event draws the perfect balance of quantity and quality attendees to maximize ROI.
From building event websites and integrating registration portals to crafting acquisition strategies and marketing assets, we handle every aspect of audience acquisition. Whether acting as an extension of your marketing team or managing the entire process, our goal is simple: bring the audience you need to your event.
Our Services Include:
- Strategic Planning
- Web Development
- Audience Acquisition Strategy
- Paid Placement
- Content Strategy & Production
- Design
- PR
- Attendee Communications
- Reporting and Optimization
Experience Design
Engaging Audiences, Driving Results
Experience design is the cornerstone of our work at GPJ, uniting strategy, creative, technology, and production to engage your target audience. It blends commerce, psychology, anthropology, and communication to create meaningful, participatory, and immersive customer interactions.
Our time-tested approach ensures optimal engagement, driving outcomes like generating new leads and capturing valuable customer insights.
Our Experience Design Services Include:
- Environmental Strategy
- Experience Design (Physical, Digital, Social, Mobile)
- Attendee Journey Mapping
- Sensory Component Design (Lighting, Sound, Texture, etc.)
- Experience Measurement Strategy
Hybrid Event Strategy & Execution
Digital & Hybrid Events: Experience-Driven, Globally Delivered
At GPJ, our “experience first” approach drives user journeys that connect and engage across event and experience portfolios. From producing digital and hybrid events since 2008 to building custom studios anywhere in the world, we bring expertise and innovation to every project.
Our live production team specializes in virtual events, including broadcasts, streaming, set design, direction, and content creation—crafted specifically for online engagement. While technology enables delivery, the experience itself drives meaningful business outcomes.
Since 2008, We’ve Delivered:
- Highly engaging virtual events that amplify your message and provide actionable analytics
- Hybrid/omni-channel events blending in-person and online strategies, like “hub and spoke” programs
- Always-on virtual platforms supporting multiple events across event portfolios
- Online event marketing integrated with social media and mobile devices
- Custom broadcast studios for HQs, satellite offices, or homes—anywhere in the world
- With over 1,200 virtual and hybrid events produced since 2020, we’re ready to help you create unforgettable experiences.
Sponsorship Sales & Partner Management
GPJ’s Sponsorship Sales and Partner Management (SPPM) team ensures your sponsorship programs are strategically designed and flawlessly executed. From developing impactful sales tools to managing sponsor relationships, we drive revenue and deliver measurable value.
Our experts handle every aspect of sponsorship—from program design and outreach to onsite execution and post-event follow-up—ensuring all benefits are delivered and obligations met.
Our SSPM Services Include:
- Strategic Planning
- Prospectus Development
- Sponsor Acquisition & Management
- Sales Tools & Outreach
- Sponsor Communications & Benefit Execution
Strategy & Planning
Strategic Experience Mapping® is GPJ’s proprietary process for uncovering deep insights into audience needs, behaviors, and preferences. Developed in the mid-1990s and refined through decades of experience across diverse industries, it lays the foundation for our award-winning creative and experience design teams.
This process produces a detailed schematic that aligns brand objectives with audience segments, outlining the content and experiential strategies needed to drive desired actions. Combined with our Portfolio Planning model, our clients have a truly powerful toolset with which to make data-driven decisions.
With the right strategy and creative execution, GPJ ensures your brand’s success through innovative, results-driven experiences.
Sustainability Planning & Execution
Driving Change Through Sustainability and Inclusion
As the world’s leading experience marketing agency, GPJ is committed to creating lasting change by delivering live, digital, and hybrid experiences that are diverse, equitable, inclusive, and sustainable.
Environmental stewardship is embedded in everything we do. From leadership to daily practices, sustainability inspires our work and informs how we help clients navigate a complex landscape. Our internal experts provide tools and measurements to design responsible, sustainable initiatives that minimize business risks and environmental impact.
When sustainability isn’t a priority for clients, we elevate the conversation. We collaborate to reduce event impacts, ask tough questions, and develop sustainability playbooks aligned with their mission and goals. Together, we’re shaping a more sustainable future for experience marketing.
Learn more about our sustainable experience practice here.
          
          
            Fearless Creativity
          
        
                  Creative Services
From Big Ideas to Brand Devotion
At GPJ, our rigorous and programmatic approach to brand experiences begins with strategy and is driven by a passion for creating unforgettable moments. We start with bold, disruptive ideas that challenge conventions and refine them through a world-class experience design process.
Our global creative studios, winners of countless industry awards, focus on building brand fans, not just customers. Trusted by the world’s most respected marketers, we transform event portfolios into high-performance marketing investments that inspire lasting loyalty.
Our Creative Services Include:
- Branding, Theme Development & Messaging
- Conference Production Design
- Copywriting
- 2D & 3D Design
- Graphic Design
- Presentation Design
- Digital Animation, Photography, & Video
- Signage & Collateral Design
Content Creation
Engaging, Immersive, Flawlessly Delivered
Whether it’s a digital experience, a high-production keynote, or a series of presentations, GPJ delivers. For over 100 years, we’ve crafted award-winning content for brand activations worldwide, including engaging presentations, immersive games, digital interfaces, and more.
Our process begins with strategy, is executed with precision design, and culminates in flawless delivery—hallmarks of the world’s leading experiential agency. Everything we create is designed to build meaningful connections with your target audience and drive lasting results.
Creative Technology
Where Creativity Meets Innovation
At GPJ, we lead the industry in creative technology for brand experiences, where data-driven strategy meets cutting-edge innovation. We craft immersive environments where brands come to life through innovative storytelling powered by experiential tech and AI.
Creative technology is the art of using digital tools to create personalized, engaging experiences that connect people with brands—both online and in real life. It combines creativity and technology to make experiences interactive, memorable, and meaningful.
From immersive games and intuitive mobile apps to dynamic user journeys, our digital programs extend and amplify your brand experience as part of a broader experience design strategy. Our transparent approach allows you to enjoy the benefits of advanced technology without worrying about the complexities.
Our Creative Technology Services Include:
- AI/Technology Consulting
- Social Media Management & Activation
- Event Gamification
- Online Broadcasts & Virtual Events
- Digital Experience Design
- Mobile Apps & Registration Technology
- Digital, Social, & Mobile Event Support
- Data Capture & Lead Generation
- Dynamic Content Management
Learn more about our Creative Technology services here.
Live Broadcast & Studio Design
Live Broadcast Streaming: Amplifying Your Brand Message
At GPJ, we’ve been using broadcast streaming to create impactful digital experiences for years, blending TV-level production quality with data-driven insights. Whether it’s a high-production online broadcast or a fast-turn virtual event, we know how to deliver content that enhances your brand and drives engagement.
Turn to GPJ for online broadcasting services that include:
- Corporate broadcast studio design and construction anywhere in the world
- High production value with expert stage design, lighting, direction, and streaming
- A one-stop shop for communications strategy, creative ideation, content development, and content strategy
          
          
            Innovative Production
          
        
                  Engineering & Fabrication
From Concept to Creation
At GPJ, we don’t just design experiences—we engineer and fabricate them with unmatched precision. As a fully vertically integrated agency, we offer the largest fabrication footprint in the industry, with facilities in Las Vegas, Nashville, Detroit, and Europe. Our scale and buying power ensure your brand activation is both cost-effective and unforgettable.
Our expert teams handle every step under one roof—from engineering and carpentry to welding, painting, and shipping. This centralized approach streamlines production, shortens turnaround times, and ensures top-tier quality and craftsmanship while increasing sustainability. It’s no wonder GPJ is consistently recognized across the industry.
See examples of our fabrication expertise here.
Event Production
Seamless Execution, Memorable Experiences
At GPJ, we know the devil is in the details. That’s why our award-winning event management team ensures every aspect of your event is flawlessly executed. From strategy to action, we create efficient, cost-conscious plans that result in beautiful, memorable, and shareable experiences—building lasting brand devotion.
We manage all facets of event production, including speaker coordination, timelines, resources and logistics. By leveraging expertise across GPJ’s disciplines, including broadcast streaming, we ensure every objective is met and every detail addressed.
Our Event Production Services Include:

- Event Broadcasting Streaming
- Live Streaming Virtual Events
- Experiential Retail

- Registration Services & Contact Center Management

Discover how GPJ brings events to life with precision and creativity.
See examples of our event production work here.
Experience Technology
The Right Technology That Enhances the Experience
Experience Technology focuses on selecting the right technology to support each experience. GPJ is platform- and vendor-agnostic, prioritizing solutions that fit the goals, audience, and scale of the project. From backend systems to hardware and software integration, this team ensures every technical choice is practical, reliable, and built for real-world execution.
See examples of our Experience Technology work here.
Graphics Production
Versatile and High-Quality Solutions
GPJ’s graphics and printing department delivers precision and creativity for all your signage and branding needs. From computer-cut vinyl lettering and logos to large-scale vehicle wraps, we handle a wide range of specialty materials and techniques for trade shows, advertising, and point-of-purchase displays.
Our capabilities include dye-sublimation printing, direct-to-textile and board printing, CNC contour routing, vinyl cutting, lamination, and fabric finishing—all completed within our state-of-the-art production facilities and with sustainability as a priority.
See examples of our graphics production here.
Third Party Vendor and Partner Management
Transparency and Commitment to Diversity
At GPJ, we pass through all third-party program costs with full transparency and no markup, ensuring the best value for our clients.
We are also deeply committed to diversity through our Minority Vendor Program, which increases opportunities for MBEs (Minority Business Enterprises) and WBEs (Women-Owned Business Enterprises). Our goal is to deliver high-quality products and services at the best possible price. If an MBE or WBE meets GPJ’s high standards, they are carefully considered for partnerships that foster mutual success.
          
          
            Specialty Services
          
        
                  Global Event Portfolio Management
Efficiency Without Compromise
Managing global event portfolios means balancing the needs of diverse business units, product leads, and country teams while delivering creative, production, and business success. At GPJ, we’ve pioneered a model that maximizes efficiency without sacrificing the innovation that drives customer engagement.
Our award-winning creative and design is fueled by strategy, and underpinned by proven processes and web-based tools that organize everything from barcode asset tracking to limiting the impact of change orders.
Our platform of global event management services helps marketers make global event programs more relevant to the CMO, the CFO and yes, the CEO, by reducing costs, through the use of our proprietary reporting and scoring program, and by showcasing ROI across the portfolio.
Learn more HERE!
Live Production
Magnifying Your Story
At GPJ, we don’t just produce events—we bring stories to life. Our industry-leading live production team specializes in transforming powerful narratives into breathtaking experiences, from immersive public ceremonies to memorable conference keynotes and spectacular entertainment.
By uniting strategy, creative, technology, and production, our live production and broadcast streaming capabilities deliver seamless, high-impact events that captivate audiences and provide peace of mind for our clients.
